sentences.text: This bulb has no battery.
No wire joins it to the supply.
So why is it glowing?
The lower coil carries alternating current, which goes back and forth fifty times a second.
So its magnetic field keeps growing, shrinking and reversing.
The iron core carries that changing field upward.
A changing magnetic field through a coil pushes a current around it.
That is electromagnetic induction.
One coil drives the other without touching it: mutual induction.
With a steady current from a cell, nothing happens.
The needle kicks only at the moment we switch on, and again when we switch off.
No change, no current.
Lift the coil and the bulb dims, because less of the field reaches it.
Double the turns, and the voltage roughly doubles.
That is how a transformer works.
Now an aluminium ring.
It is a coil with just one turn.
The induced current makes the ring a magnet that opposes the coil, and it jumps.
Cut a slot in the ring and it stays put.
No complete path, no current, no force.
Chargers, transformers and induction cooktops all use this.
Next: why does the ring get hot?
